_note: Slide 16, corrected to what OpenSearch actually ships. Two changes from the slide: (1) there is no 'enrich' processor in OpenSearch, so asset ownership is applied by the generated stored script 'asset-owner-lookup'; (2) the fingerprint processor takes 'hash_method' with a version-suffixed value ('SHA-1@2.16.0'), not 'method': 'SHA-1'. Enrichment is cheap here at write time and ruinous at query time.
description: Normalise and enrich security logs and agent traces (Chasing shadows demo)

community_id._note: OpenSearch 2.13+. bin/bootstrap.py checks _nodes/ingest and swaps this for a fingerprint-based flow key if the processor is unavailable.

script._note: Stands in for slide 16's enrich processor, which OpenSearch does not have. The asset inventory is compiled into this processor's params by bin/bootstrap.py from the asset-owner index, so ownership is still resolved once at write time rather than joined at query time. Re-run bootstrap when the inventory changes; in production you would regenerate this pipeline from your CMDB on a schedule, or carry ownership on the span from the collector.
script.source: def rec = params.owners.get(ctx.cloud.instance.id); if (rec == null) { return; } if (ctx.asset == null) { ctx.asset = new HashMap(); } ctx.asset.owner = rec[0]; ctx.asset.team = rec[1]; ctx.asset.criticality = rec[2];

fingerprint._note: flow.id - one identifier for a conversation between two endpoints, so a pivot across every IP an attacker rotates through is a term query.
context.hash - fingerprint of the fetched document. One term query lists every agent that ingested the same poison. This is the field that turned a six-hour incident into a 52-minute one.

drop._note: Drop what no detector reads. Sub-64-byte flow records are keepalives.
Successful chat spans that produced almost nothing are the bulk of the agent firehose and no detector reads them.

remove._note: Store the projection, not the prompt (slide 18). The window of gaps existed only to produce pace_cv; the fetched document existed only to produce context.hash. Both leave before the document is written - the body lives in sec-context-docs, keyed by that hash. Remove the whole gen_ai.tool.input OBJECT, not just the .document leaf: removing the leaf leaves an empty {} behind in _source, which looks like the body is still there.
